platforms.name: Papyrus
platforms.summary: Customer-hosted agentic workspace for document automation, internal app creation and legacy system enablement.

capabilities.value: Document automation, internal app creation and legacy system enablement with governed agent execution.
capabilities.caveat: Describes intended scope in Beag Labs' own words; it is not an independent test of output quality.

deployment.value: Customer-hosted: a Papyrus VM in the customer's Azure subscription, or on-premises, restricted or disconnected environments.
deployment.caveat: Supported environments and versions should be confirmed against the current agreement and documentation.

marketplaceOffer.value: Azure Marketplace private offer that deploys the Papyrus VM into the customer's subscription.
marketplaceOffer.caveat: Private offer, not a public self-serve listing; the signed entitlement remains customer-specific.

humanApproval.value: Governed execution: consequential actions are reviewed and work stays visible as it progresses.
humanApproval.caveat: The page does not enumerate which actions require approval or the approval workflow; confirm details before relying on it for a specific control.

licensing.value: Commercial: a signed organization license (offline) or a customer-specific Azure private offer.
licensing.caveat: Papyrus is not offered under an open-source license on this page. Third-party component licenses are listed separately in the Trust Center SBOM.

security.value: 35 OSCAL control implementations: project-scoped RBAC, hash-linked audit records, OIDC/SAML/WebAuthn and CAC/PIV sign-in by profile.
security.caveat: A self-published control mapping, not a third-party assessment, certification or authorization to operate. Customers retain responsibility for configuration.

buyer.value: Organizations that need back office automation on their own infrastructure, in business and government settings.

pricing.value: No public price card; commercial terms are scoped to the deployment.
pricing.caveat: Establishes that no public price is published, not what a deployment costs.

bestFor.text: Teams that must keep agent execution inside their own Azure subscription or a disconnected environment.
Buyers who need a published, machine-readable control mapping to review during procurement.

lessSuitedFor.text: Teams that want a free, open-source licence or public per-seat pricing to evaluate without talking to sales.

platforms.notes: Beag Labs makes Papyrus. Every Papyrus cell cites Beag Labs' own pages and is labelled first-party.

platforms.name: Corral AI (identified as 'Corral Sovereign AI')
platforms.summary: Corral AI is described by its vendor as an AI foundation deployed from Azure Marketplace into the customer's own Azure tenant, where agents are built and governed.

capabilities.value: Deploy into your cloud, connect data, build agents via Agent Builder; per-user Hub assistant, embeddable widgets.
capabilities.caveat: Vendor marketing; no independent test of functionality.

deployment.value: Deploys into the customer's own Azure tenant and subscription; AWS and GCP listed as coming 2026.
deployment.caveat: Vendor says Corral manages updates/monitoring (launch post); AWS/GCP not yet available per page.

marketplaceOffer.value: Vendor site links a 'Corral AI managed app' Azure Marketplace listing (azure-application URL path).
marketplaceOffer.caveat: Marketplace page itself returned HTTP 403 to fetch, so the listing content was not independently read.

humanApproval.value: Admin approval gates the agent publish flow, and high-risk actions need a human after untrusted content; other actions are not described.
humanApproval.caveat: Vendor description; configurability of gates not verified.

licensing.value: Not found in checked official pages.
licensing.caveat: Pages mention a platform subscription via marketplace but state no license model.

security.value: Documented: on-tenant residency, private endpoints/VNet, immutable audit trail, content filtering/PII detection, identity-provider governance.
security.caveat: Security page names no SSO/RBAC/encryption; home page claims Entra ID SSO/RBAC. Says it inherits Azure certifications; Corral's own certifications not stated.

buyer.value: Lists Ops & Product Teams, IT & Security Teams, Developers, Service Providers/SIs, Product Companies.

pricing.value: No prices listed; platform subscription plus Azure infra costs via Marketplace, counting toward MACC; Enterprise plan via 'Talk to us'.
pricing.caveat: No amounts published; Marketplace plan prices not read.

bestFor.text: Buyers who need the AI runtime inside their own Azure tenant
Buyers wanting Azure Marketplace procurement against existing Azure commitments

lessSuitedFor.text: Buyers needing AWS or GCP deployment today

platforms.notes: Product found as 'Corral AI' (getcorral.ai); vendor page does not use the term 'Sovereign AI' as a product name (section 'Control & Sovereignty'). Identification as the intended product is probable but unconfirmed. Marketplace listing returned 403. Launch post dated 2024-12-15.

platforms.name: HeartBeatAgents
platforms.summary: HeartBeatAgents is a self-hosted platform for building and running autonomous AI agents that work on standing orders with local memory.

capabilities.value: Autonomous agents on standing orders with tools, integrations, three-layer local memory, and reusable skills.

deployment.value: Self-hosted: desktop download (macOS DMG) on vendor site; AWS listing ships an AMI run in buyer's AWS account.
deployment.caveat: Two different delivery forms; AWS AMI is not Azure.

marketplaceOffer.value: No Azure Marketplace listing found; only an AWS Marketplace AMI listing was found.
marketplaceOffer.caveat: Absence of a found listing does not prove none exists; Microsoft Marketplace was searched only via web search.

humanApproval.value: Only simple 'Ask User' and 'Present Choices' skills let an agent request approval or a choice; no broader approval policy is described.
humanApproval.caveat: No broader approval workflow/policy gates described; security page describes none.

licensing.value: AWS listing: EULA applies; community edition with one worker, more workers via separately purchased license.
licensing.caveat: Source-code license (open or not) not stated.

security.value: Documented: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+, per-organization container folder scoping, token-authenticated websockets, token scrubbing.
security.caveat: SSO, RBAC, certifications and audit log content/retention not documented there.

buyer.value: AWS listing targets organizations wanting production-ready self-hosted agentic AI infrastructure.
buyer.caveat: Vendor site does not name a buyer persona.

pricing.value: No prices listed; AWS listing says community edition with one worker, billing external via vendor license.
pricing.caveat: Vendor pricing page rendered empty on fetch.

bestFor.text: Teams wanting agents run on their own machine or AWS account

lessSuitedFor.text: Buyers who need to purchase through Azure Marketplace: we found no Azure listing in the sources checked (an AWS Marketplace listing exists).

platforms.notes: Product exists (heartbeatagents.com, Mosaic Singularity). No Azure Marketplace listing found; the only marketplace listing found is AWS. Some Microsoft Marketplace pages returned for searches were for an unrelated product (Fellowmind HiveAI). Task premise of Azure listing is unverified.

platforms.name: OpenClaw
platforms.vendor: OpenClaw Foundation (independent nonprofit, per repo README)
platforms.summary: OpenClaw is an open-source assistant/gateway that runs on your own machine or server and connects chat apps to AI agents (repo README; docs.openclaw.ai).

capabilities.value: Single Gateway links chat channels to AI agents with tools, sessions, memory, skills, cron/webhooks, a web Control UI, and mobile nodes.
capabilities.caveat: Describes features, not their quality, scale, or reliability.

deployment.value: Runs on your own laptop or server; install via script, npm, Docker, Nix or source; remote access via SSH/Tailscale. README says no hosted service.
deployment.caveat: Does not cover third-party hosted or marketplace deployments of the software.

marketplaceOffer.value: No official Azure/Microsoft Marketplace listing found in first-party pages. A web search surfaced third-party publisher listings (not fetched; unverified).
marketplaceOffer.caveat: Third-party publishers appear to list OpenClaw offers on Microsoft Marketplace; direct fetch returned 403, so offer type, affiliation and pricing are unverified. Failed search is not proof of absence.

humanApproval.value: Exec approvals (deny, allowlist, ask, auto, full) gate host command execution only and can be switched off; not a general approval layer.
humanApproval.caveat: SECURITY.md says approvals are operator guardrails, not a multi-tenant authorization control. Covers host command execution, not every agent action.

licensing.caveat: Only the root LICENSE was read; subdirectories or plugins on ClawHub may carry other licenses. Not legal advice.

security.value: Gateway auth, DM pairing and allowlists, optional sandboxing (off by default) and an audit CLI; documented as a single-trusted-operator model, not a multi-tenant boundary.
security.caveat: SECURITY.md states it is not a multi-tenant boundary and exec runs on host by default. SSO, RBAC and audit-log features were not found on pages read (not a statement they are absent). No certifications checked.

buyer.value: Individuals wanting a personal assistant, teams sharing a gateway, and enterprise/security teams hardening via configuration, not a separate edition.
buyer.caveat: Project positioning only; no procurement or support terms stated.

pricing.value: README says no paid tier, hosted service, or token. Model API and hosting costs are borne by the user.
pricing.caveat: Says nothing about third-party managed offers, support contracts, or underlying model/hosting cost amounts.

bestFor.text: Individuals or small teams wanting a self-run assistant reachable through existing chat apps at no license cost.
Operators who want configurable command-approval gates (allowlist/ask modes) on host execution.

lessSuitedFor.text: Mutually untrusted multi-tenant use on one gateway; the project's trust model targets a single trusted operator.
Buyers needing a vendor-hosted or vendor-supported managed service from the project itself; none is offered per README.

platforms.notes: Identified as github.com/openclaw/openclaw (README, MIT LICENSE, SECURITY.md fetched). Origin story (Clawdbot/Moltbot) came only from a third-party search summary; not used. Third-party Microsoft Marketplace listings (e.g. Forceworks 'RapidClaw', Questlab, Elania Resources) were seen in search results only; marketplace page returned 403 so unverified. Star counts vary by source; omitted.

platforms.name: OpenHands
platforms.vendor: OpenHands (company name not stated on pages fetched)
platforms.summary: OpenHands is an open-source platform for software-engineering agents, with a GUI, CLI, SDK and enterprise control plane (openhands.dev).

capabilities.value: Coding agents via Agent Canvas (browser client), Software Agent SDK/Agent Server, CLI, plus scheduled/webhook automations.
capabilities.caveat: Feature description only; the Local GUI is described as deprecated in favor of Agent Canvas, which the repo labels beta.

deployment.value: Local/self-hosted (npm, Docker), plus OpenHands Cloud (managed) and OpenHands Enterprise (licensed self-host in your VPC or managed).
deployment.caveat: Customer-tenant deployment is listed under the commercial Enterprise plan only.

marketplaceOffer.value: No Azure/Microsoft Marketplace listing found for OpenHands in first-party pages or search.
marketplaceOffer.caveat: A failed search is not proof no listing exists; the marketplace was not searched directly.

humanApproval.value: SDK confirmation policies (always, never, risky) can require approval of actions; documented for the SDK, and one call path bypasses them.
humanApproval.caveat: Documented for the SDK; the page says execute_tool() bypasses these controls. Not checked for Cloud/Canvas UI or defaults.

licensing.value: Root LICENSE of OpenHands/OpenHands is MIT (OpenHands contributors, 2025). Docs say each repository has its own license.
licensing.caveat: Not verified: the SDK repo license, and whether an enterprise directory carries a different license (enterprise/LICENSE URL returned 404). OpenHands Cloud/Enterprise are commercial offerings.

security.value: Docs name: Docker sandbox isolation for the agent server, security analyzers with risk levels, Enterprise SAML/SSO, RBAC and access controls (Cloud).
security.caveat: SECURITY.md returned 404, so no vulnerability-disclosure policy was found. Pricing page does not explicitly tie RBAC to a tier. Audit logging, certifications not found on pages read.

buyer.value: Developers and engineering teams, including enterprises wanting control over models, data, access and auditability.

pricing.value: Local open source: free. SaaS Individual: free, 10 daily conversations. Enterprise: custom pricing, contact sales.
pricing.caveat: Enterprise price, SLA and contract terms not published. Model usage at cost or BYOK; amounts not stated in fetched summary. Page may have other tiers not captured.

bestFor.text: Engineering teams wanting a coding-focused agent they can run locally or self-host with free open-source options.
Developers embedding agents with configurable approve/reject gates via the SDK.

lessSuitedFor.text: Buyers needing published Enterprise pricing or SLA terms up front; these are contact-sales.
Buyers needing a general personal-assistant across chat apps; the project is positioned for software engineering.

platforms.notes: Identified via openhands.dev, docs.openhands.dev, github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands. The fetched repo README/page now describes Agent Canvas (labeled beta) as the browser client; the repo README showed no license section but the LICENSE file is MIT. Former name OpenDevin / All-Hands-AI not verified on a fetched page. Enterprise directory license not verified.

platforms.name: Websoft9
platforms.summary: Websoft9 is a self-hosted PaaS and app store for deploying and managing 300+ open source apps on one server.

capabilities.value: App store with one-click install of 300+ apps, plus app lifecycle, file manager, terminal, proxy/SSL, backups, monitoring.
capabilities.caveat: Platform for deploying other apps; no AI-agent features documented on pages checked; AI agents would depend on deployed third-party apps.

deployment.value: Self-hosted on your own server, running as Docker containers.
deployment.caveat: Does not describe managed hosting options in detail (pricing page mentions private cloud and managed hosting via customer success).

marketplaceOffer.value: Docs say Websoft9 is an Azure Marketplace partner; products are VM images deployed to an Azure VM.
marketplaceOffer.caveat: Page is for version 1.0, flagged by the site as no longer actively maintained; Marketplace listing page itself returned HTTP 403 so was not read.

humanApproval.value: No approval or human-in-the-loop controls documented for agent actions.
humanApproval.caveat: Platform has no documented agent-action concept.

licensing.value: Repository states LGPL-3.0 and homepage says 100% open source; republishing images to cloud marketplaces without authorization is prohibited.
licensing.caveat: License badge and text are inconsistent (LGPL vs GPL link); read the repository license file before relying on it.

security.value: Multi-user accounts with role-based access; SSL certificates via Let's Encrypt; apps isolated through Docker.
security.caveat: No SSO, audit logging, data residency or certifications documented on pages checked; role definitions not described.

buyer.value: Cloud architects, IT teams and SMBs without dedicated IT, plus software vendors, integrators and cloud providers.

pricing.value: Software plans: Free 0, Starter CNY 20/mo, Standard CNY 99/mo (per vendor pricing page); Azure image billing not described.
pricing.caveat: Pricing page is in CNY and is for support subscriptions; Azure Marketplace VM/image pricing not verified.

bestFor.text: Teams wanting to self-host many open source apps on their own server.

lessSuitedFor.text: Buyers needing documented approval gates or audit logging for agent actions; these are not documented.

platforms.notes: Websoft9 is an app store/hosting panel, not an AI agent product; no AI features documented beyond homepage category titles. Azure Marketplace pages (marketplace.microsoft.com and azuremarketplace.microsoft.com) returned HTTP 403 to fetches; search results indicate listing URL marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/virtual-machines/websoft9inc.websoft9 but it is not verified and azureMarketplaceUrl is left null. Docs for version 2.0 Azure install page not found (404).
